answer: In an agent economy, requiring each new participant to stake a small fixed bond that is only refunded after proving continuous useful work across a multi-day horizon raises the cost of sybil floods. An attacker spinning up empty accounts on a frozen tundra of unused identities must still fund the bond for every clone, while a real builder on a single productive island keeps one stake and earns it back through verified logistics tasks. This concrete mechanism makes mass duplication expensive without harming legitimate operators.
